# Rappel

> Spaced repetition flashcards at https://rappel.neorgon.com/. Loads a deck from
> one JSON document, schedules it with FSRS-6, and keeps the review ledger in
> the visitor's own browser. Any site can embed a deck in an iframe and read the
> answers back over postMessage. No account, no server, nothing uploaded.

## Writing a deck file

Produce ONE JSON object in the `neo-deck/1` format. Minimal viable deck:

    {
      "format": "neo-deck/1",
      "id": "es-core-50",
      "version": "2026-09-04",
      "name": "Spanish core 50",
      "lang": { "front": "es", "back": "en" },
      "fields": ["Word", "Meaning"],
      "templates": [
        { "id": "recognition", "kind": "basic", "skill": "es.vocab.read",
          "front": "{{Word}}", "back": "{{Meaning}}" }
      ],
      "notes": [
        { "id": "n_0001", "f": { "Word": "el perro", "Meaning": "the dog" },
          "tags": ["animals"] }
      ]
    }

Top-level fields:

- format (required) "neo-deck/1"
- id (required) starts with a letter or digit, then letters, digits, dot, dash,
  underscore. It is what the review ledger is keyed by, so never change it on
  an existing deck
- version (required) a YYYY-MM-DD date, bumped on any content change
- name (required) a string, or an { "en": ..., "es": ... } object. English is
  the fallback, then Spanish. `"es": null` means "not translated"
- lang (required) { "front": "es", "back": "en" }
- licence (SPDX id) plus attribution (the exact on-screen wording) plus
  screen ("required" or "none"). If licence starts with CC-BY then attribution
  and screen: "required" are mandatory, and the wording is rendered below the
  review area on every screen that shows the deck, in the embed too
- source (URL) where the licence text lives, linked next to the attribution
- media_base a RELATIVE path, no leading slash, no scheme and no ".." segment
- fields (required) the field names, unique, in order
- templates (required) see below
- notes (required) see below

### Templates

`kind` is one of four and nothing else. There is no template language: `{{Field}}`
substitution only. No conditionals, no filters, no `{{FrontSide}}`, no
`{{hint:}}`, no `{{tts:}}`. A literal `<br>` in a template becomes a line break;
every other piece of markup is escaped.

- basic: `front` and `back`, both `{{Field}}` strings
- typed: `answer_field` (a declared field), `front`, `back`, optional
  `transform` ("kana" or "kana-katakana"), optional `compare`
- cloze: `text_field` (a declared field holding `{{c1::text}}` or
  `{{c1::text::hint}}` markers)
- choice: `answer_field`, optional `distractors` ("siblings", the default, or
  "sample-from-deck"), optional `count` from 2 to 8, default 4. Siblings are
  notes sharing a tag with the card's note; when there are too few, the rest
  are sampled from the deck so the card is still answerable

Every template should carry `skill`, a dotted string such as
`kana.hiragana.read`. It is what an embedding host receives on every answer, so
a template with no skill makes the embed contract useless to that host. The
validator warns on a missing skill and does not refuse the deck. A note may
carry its own `skill`, which wins over the template's for that note's cards.

`compare` is a pipe separated token list applied in order, default `trim|casefold`:
`trim`, `casefold`, `strip-accents`, `collapse-space`, `kana` (both sides are
converted to hiragana before comparing).

`transform` converts romaji as the learner types (wanakana, vendored): a
trailing `n` is held back so `na` stays reachable, `nn` before a consonant is
one `n`, and the box is settled once at submit before `compare` runs. So
`onna` grades as おんな and `shinbun` as しんぶん.

### Notes and card identity

**A card is `noteId + ":" + templateId`, a string.** It is never an array index
and never a generated integer, which is what lets a reader re-download an edited
deck without losing a single review. A cloze note expands to one card per
distinct marker, so `{{c1::}}` and `{{c2::}}` in note `n_0001` under template
`gap` are `n_0001:gap:1` and `n_0001:gap:2`. A note id therefore may not
contain a colon.

Extending a deck therefore KEEPS every existing note id. Renumbering notes
discards the reader's progress on every one of them.

`f` holds the field values, all strings, and every key must be a declared field.
`tags` is optional and is what "siblings" distractors are drawn from. `templates`
is optional and limits a note to a subset of the deck's templates.

### Media

A filename reference, never inline base64, and Anki's two spellings are kept
verbatim so a converted deck needs no field rewriting:

    "Audio": "[sound:perro.mp3]"
    "Picture": "<img src=\"perro.png\">"

Both resolve against `media_base`. `[sound:]` renders as a Play button and
`<img>` as an image. An absolute URL, a root path or a `..` segment in either is
dropped rather than fetched. Every other piece of field text is escaped, so a
deck cannot inject markup into the page that reads it.

### Where a fetched deck is stored

A deck fetched from `?src=` on an origin other than `neorgon.com` or one of its
subdomains is stored, and reported in every message, as

    ext:<first 12 hex of SHA-256 of the src URL>:<deck.id>

so a third-party document claiming `"id": "jp-first-words"` cannot merge into
the reader's progress on the built-in deck of that name. Built-in decks and
decks served from `*.neorgon.com` keep their plain `id`. A host embedding its
own deck should expect the `ext:` form in `deckId`.

## Other input formats

Import also reads TSV and CSV using Anki's own header dialect verbatim, so a
file exported from Anki loads unchanged and a file exported from here imports
into Anki:

    #separator:tab
    #html:false
    #notetype:Basic
    #deck:Spanish core 50
    #columns:GUID	Front	Back	Tags
    #guid column:1
    #tags column:4

`#guid column` is what lets a person edit the file and re-import it without
duplicating notes (the value is kept as the note id after stripping anything
outside letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore). Without `#columns` the
columns are called Front, Back, Field 3 and so on; without `#separator` the
delimiter is detected from the first line. A bare two-column paste with no
header block works. A row whose first column is empty is skipped. The imported
deck gets `licence: "unspecified"`, `screen: "none"`, today's date as its
version and a slug of `#deck` as its id.

JSON import accepts a `neo-deck/1` document, an array of objects (the union of
their keys becomes the field list), or an array of two-item arrays (Front and
Back).

**`.apkg` is not supported and will not be.** The modern inner collection is
zstd compressed and `DecompressionStream("zstd")` exists only in Firefox 138 and
later, and the SQLite reader that would be needed is 0.69 MB of third-party
runtime. Export from Anki as a text file instead.

## The scheduler

FSRS-6 with the 21 published default parameters, transcribed from `fsrs-rs`
6.6.2. Ratings are 1 Again, 2 Hard, 3 Good, 4 Easy.

**Hard is a passing grade.** It means you recalled the answer and it took
effort. Pressing Hard when you did not recall the answer at all makes every
future interval too long. Again is the button for a failure.

There is no parameter optimizer here: fitting parameters is gradient descent
over the entire review history and needs a build step this site does not have.
Settings accepts a pasted array of 17, 19 or 21 numbers, migrated the way
`fsrs-rs` migrates a short one, and checked for length and finiteness only.

Learning steps default to 60 and 600 seconds, relearning to 600, and the study
day rolls over at 04:00 local. Every answer writes an absolute due timestamp, so
closing the tab mid-step loses nothing. A review session shows learning cards,
then due cards, then up to 20 new cards (or `limit`, when given).

## Storage, and what is honest about it

- The card map (stability, difficulty, due date, reps, lapses per card) is in
  `localStorage` under `rappel:ledger:v1`. Rappel refuses to add a deck that
  would push it past 1.5 MiB and says so with the number.
- The review log is append-only in IndexedDB, database `rappel`, store
  `reviews`, keyed by deck and timestamp. It is not in localStorage because
  writing it there would cost a full rewrite of the whole history on every
  single answer.
- Decks you import are in `localStorage` under `rappel:decks:v1`. Scheduler
  settings are under `rappel:prefs:v1` and the in-progress session under
  `rappel:session:v1`, so a closed tab resumes where it was.
- A personal deck (below) is in `rappel:decks:v1` with the others, and which
  site sent it, and when, is under `rappel:personal:v1`.
- Nothing is uploaded. Export writes both halves into one `neo-ledger/1`
  document, and Restore takes one back in, merging per card by whichever review
  is newer. The `scheduler` block in an imported ledger is validated and not
  applied: a document never sets a reader's memory parameters.

## Embedding (iframe)

Any site can embed a deck. The contract version is `neo-rappel-embed/1`.

    <iframe src="https://rappel.neorgon.com/?embed=1&mode=review&limit=20&src=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fdeck.json"
      width="100%" height="640" loading="lazy" style="border:0"
      title="Spanish core 50 · Rappel"></iframe>

URL parameters:

- `embed=1` strips the chrome to a slim bar with an "Open in Rappel" link,
  preserving the other parameters in the escape URL except `embed` and
  `ledger`, so the top-level page persists normally
- `deck=<id>` selects a deck Rappel already ships
- `deck=personal:<...>` names a personal deck the host sends with `rappel:load`
  (below). If the engine already holds that id the frame is ready at once with
  the stored copy; if not, it shows a waiting line and posts nothing until the
  deck arrives. No `no-deck` error, no timeout: only the host can end the wait
- `src=<https URL>` fetches a `neo-deck/1` document, which needs CORS. Plain
  `http://localhost` is accepted only when the engine itself is on localhost
- `#d=<base64url(deck json)>` carries the deck in the fragment instead, UTF-8
- `mode=review | cram | browse`, default `review`. **`cram` writes nothing to
  the ledger**: it runs every card, shuffled, and schedules none of them
- `limit=<N>` caps the session. A value that is not a finite positive number is
  discarded
- `ledger=engine | host`, default `engine`. `host` makes the frame fully
  in-memory and hands you the whole ledger on `rappel:progress`. See the
  section on `?ledger=` below
- `lang=en | es`
- `theme=<name>` applies a fleet theme

Exactly one of `deck`, `src` or `#d=` must be present. Zero is
`rappel:error { code: "no-deck" }`. More than one takes them in that order and
names the ignored ones on the console. In embed mode a session starts on load;
`mode=browse` lists the cards instead.

### Messages the engine sends you

Every message is `{ v: 1, type, ... }` and is posted to your origin (the
referrer's origin), never `*`. With no referrer the engine posts nothing.
**Ignore any message whose `v` you do not recognise.**

- `rappel:ready` `{ deckId, deckVersion, name, total, due, new, ledger }`.
  `ledger` is `"engine"` or `"ephemeral"`. Fires on load once a deck resolved,
  and again every time you send `rappel:hello`
- `rappel:due` `{ deckId, due, new, learning, total, nextDueAt }`. On ready,
  after every session end, and after a restore lands. `nextDueAt` is a
  timestamp in ms or null
- `rappel:session-start` `{ deckId, sessionId, queued }`
- `rappel:answer` `{ deckId, sessionId, cardId, itemId, skill, grade, correct, ms }`,
  one per graded card, in cram mode too. `cardId` is `noteId:templateId`;
  `itemId` is `deckId + ":" + noteId`, one per note rather than per card, so
  a recognition card and a recall card of the same word share it. `grade` is
  1 to 4. `correct` is whether the typed or picked answer matched for a typed
  or choice card (after the transform's settle step and `compare`), and
  `grade >= 2` otherwise. `ms` is time from showing the card to grading it
- `rappel:session-end` `{ deckId, sessionId, answered, again, hard, good, easy, ms, due, new }`
- `rappel:progress` `{ deckId, format: "neo-ledger/1", ledger }`. Sent in reply
  to `rappel:export`, and under `ledger=host` after every answer and every
  session end, log included
- `rappel:error` `{ code, message }`. Codes: `no-deck`, `deck-fetch-failed`,
  `deck-invalid`, `storage-unavailable`, `origin-refused`. A `rappel:restore`
  whose document fails validation is reported as `deck-invalid` with the
  validator's message. `storage-unavailable` is reserved: the current engine
  reports a failed storage probe as `ledger: "ephemeral"` on `rappel:ready`
  rather than as an error
- `rappel:resize` `{ height }`

**If you stop receiving `rappel:answer`, nothing looks broken.** The frame keeps
showing a working deck and you quietly stop recording anything. That is why
every message carries a version and why you should treat a long silence after
`rappel:session-start` as a fault rather than as an idle learner.

### Messages you can send the engine

Every inbound message must carry `v: 1` and a `type` starting with `rappel:`;
anything else is dropped without a reply.

- `rappel:hello` `{ v: 1 }`. The engine re-emits `rappel:ready`. **Send this on
  the iframe's load event.** The engine can become ready before you attach your
  listener, and without this your panel is intermittently blank
- `rappel:start` `{ limit?, mode? }`. Starts or restarts a session; `mode`
  defaults to `review`
- `rappel:export` `{ log?: boolean }`. `log` defaults false, because a
  100,000-entry log is 8 MiB of postMessage
- `rappel:restore` `{ format: "neo-ledger/1", ledger, strategy: "merge" | "replace" }`
- `rappel:theme` `{ theme }`. A name of up to 32 letters, digits, `_` or `-`
- `rappel:load` `{ deck, store?: "engine" | "ephemeral" }`. `deck` is a whole
  `neo-deck/1` document, `store` defaults to `"engine"`. Post it on the
  iframe's load event, then `rappel:hello`

Two of these can write: `rappel:restore` and `rappel:load`. Both are accepted
from `neorgon.com` and its subdomains over https (and from `localhost` when the
engine itself is on `localhost`). From any other origin a restore is accepted
only when the frame is not persisting, that is under `ledger=host` or after a
failed storage probe, where it writes nothing but memory; otherwise it is
refused with `rappel:error { code: "origin-refused" }`. A load from any other
origin is not refused: it is renamed under a hash of that origin and held in
memory for the life of the frame, which arrives at the same guarantee by a
different route. An unlisted origin can never
cause a write to `rappel.neorgon.com`'s persistent storage, and deleting counts
as writing: a deck the engine may not keep can neither save nor clear the saved
session of a deck it did keep.

    const RAPPEL = 'https://rappel.neorgon.com';
    window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
      if (e.origin !== RAPPEL) return;
      const m = e.data;
      if (!m || m.v !== 1) return;
      if (m.type === 'rappel:ready')  { showDue(m.due); if (m.ledger === 'ephemeral') warnNotSaved(); }
      if (m.type === 'rappel:answer') { record(m.itemId, m.skill, m.correct, m.ms); }
    });
    frame.addEventListener('load', () => {
      frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ v: 1, type: 'rappel:hello' }, RAPPEL);
    });

### What `rappel:restore` does with the document

- It is validated as `neo-ledger/1` first: `format`, `exported` (a timestamp
  in ms), `origin` (the exporting origin), a `scheduler` block with `name:
  "fsrs"`, `version: 6`, 21 finite `w`, `desired_retention` between 0.5 and 1,
  `maximum_interval` (a whole number of days, at least 1), `learn_steps`,
  `relearn_steps`, `day_start_hour`, and `decks` keyed by deck
  id with a `cards` map keyed by `noteId:templateId`. The document you get on
  `rappel:progress` already has this shape; send it back as it came
- `merge` (the default) is last-write-wins per card by `lr`, the last review
  timestamp: a card lands only when it is absent here or its `lr` is strictly
  newer, so two devices reviewing different cards lose nothing. `replace`
  drops the local card map first
- `log` entries are appended to the review log, keyed by deck and timestamp, so
  sending the same document twice is a no-op rather than a duplicate. A frame
  that cannot persist (`ledger=host`, or a failed probe) ignores the log half of
  a restore and merges only the card rows, into memory
- The `scheduler` block is validated and never applied. The frame's own
  parameters are untouched by a restore
- There is no dedicated acknowledgement. After a restore lands the frame
  re-renders and posts `rappel:due`; a rejected one posts `rappel:error` with
  code `deck-invalid` and the first validation message

### What `rappel:load` does with the document

- It goes through the same door as a fetched deck: validated as `neo-deck/1`,
  then checked against the card map ceiling. A document that fails is refused
  with `rappel:error { code: "deck-invalid" }` and the first validation
  message, and nothing of it is kept. Over the ceiling is `storage-unavailable`
- From `neorgon.com`, its subdomains over https, or `localhost` when the
  engine is on `localhost`, the deck keeps its own `id`. From any other origin
  it is renamed `ext:<12 hex of SHA-256 of your origin>:<id>` and lives in
  memory only
- **It is stored, and its scheduling written to this engine's ledger, only when
  your origin is one of those, `store` is `"engine"`, and the frame is itself
  persisting** (`ledger=engine` and the boot probe passed). Otherwise the deck
  and every grade on it live for the life of the frame. An unlisted origin can
  never cause a write to `rappel.neorgon.com`'s persistent storage; that rule
  did not move
- The reply is `rappel:ready`, then `rappel:due`, exactly as after a load from
  the URL. `ledger` on that ready is `"engine"` when the deck was stored and
  `"ephemeral"` when it was not, so one field tells you which world you got
- Sending the same `id` again with a newer `version` replaces the notes and
  templates. Every card whose `noteId:templateId` still exists keeps its
  stability, difficulty, due date, reps and lapses untouched. A card whose id
  is gone loses its row (the same sweep a re-downloaded deck gets); its
  reviews stay in the log, and if the id ever comes back it starts as new. The
  same `version` is a no-op and an older one is ignored with a console line;
  both re-emit `rappel:ready` with what is stored
- `version` on a `personal:` deck may be `YYYY-MM-DD.N`, `N` a whole number,
  so a host that rebuilds several times a day has an order finer than the
  date. Newer means a later date, else the same date and a greater `N`
- Under `mode=cram` the document is still kept when the rules above allow it;
  cram writes no scheduling, as before

### `?ledger=`: where the ledger lives in an embed, stated honestly

By default (`ledger=engine`) the frame writes to `rappel.neorgon.com`'s own
storage, so a person embedding a deck on a `neorgon.com` site shares one ledger
with standalone Rappel. That is a **same-site guarantee only**. Browsers
partition third-party storage by the top-level site, so a deck embedded on your
own domain gets its own partition and its own ledger, and Safari may partition
even the same-site case. The engine probes both `localStorage` and IndexedDB at
boot, before anything is written or posted, and tells you which world you are
in on `rappel:ready`: `"engine"` when it can persist, `"ephemeral"` when it
cannot.

`ledger=host` makes the frame ephemeral on purpose:

- nothing is written to `localStorage` or IndexedDB, not the card map, not the
  log, not the settings, not the session
- `rappel:ready` reports `ledger: "ephemeral"`
- `rappel:progress` fires with the full log after every answer and every
  session end, because on unload the frame's memory is gone
- `rappel:restore` is accepted from any origin, since it can only reach memory
- the "Open in Rappel" link drops `ledger` from the URL, so the top-level page
  persists normally

If progress matters to you, use `?ledger=host`, keep the latest
`rappel:progress` document yourself, and push it back with `rappel:restore` on
the next load (after `rappel:ready`, when the deck has resolved). And leave the
"Open in Rappel" link in place: the top-level origin is the one path that
always works.

## Personal decks

A deck whose `id` starts with `personal:` is one another site built from your
own answers and sent with `rappel:load`; Runcible's "Your misses" is one. The
id is `personal:<site>:<...>`, the second segment being the sending site's own
name, and the prefix is reserved: a built-in deck, a `?src=` deck or a `#d=`
deck carrying it is refused by the validator.

- It shows in the library under its own heading, "Personal decks", with the
  name the sending site gave it, and one line saying which site sent it and
  when. It is never listed among the decks this build ships
- Its scheduling exports and restores in `neo-ledger/1` like any other deck's,
  keyed by its id. The document itself is not in a ledger export, the same as
  an imported deck: the site that built it sends it again
- Forget removes the document and its rows from this browser and does not stop
  the sending site from sending it again on its next visit
- Opened standalone (`?deck=personal:...`) it is the stored copy; with none
  stored, the library opens with one line saying the deck is not here and to
  open it from the site that built it

## Keyboard

Space shows the answer. 1 to 4 grade it. `?` opens the full shortcut sheet, `H`
hides the chrome (standalone only; there is no chrome to hide in an embed), `G`
jumps to another Neorgon site.
